title: Map curve
tagline: Carry a span from one chain onto another by arc length from a reference point: s mm along the first from its zero lands s mm along the second from its zero.

slides.title: What it does
slides.problem: The same stations are needed on different curves of a ski -- the RSL, the side profile, the core bottom -- measured along each curve from the same place (the FCP). Trim and split work by position, not by distance along the curve. Map curve measures along both chains from a zero point.
useWhen: A span defined on one curve is needed on another
Distances must follow the curve, not X
Arcs must stay arcs (Trim mode never refits)
slides.caption: SKI_PROFILE trimmed to the RSL span, measured along it from the FCP.

slides.title: Arc length from a zero point

points.head: Same distance along each
points.body: The from-chain's span [start, end], measured from its zero, is laid onto the to-chain from its zero.

points.head: World X or closest
points.body: World X: the zero lands where each chain crosses the point's X. Closest point: the nearest point on each chain.

points.head: Direction check
points.body: If the chains run opposite ways at the zero, the feature stops and asks for Flip to-chain.

slides.title: The dialog
params: Deform from-edges onto to-edges / TRIM to-edges to the from span / Deform and merge to one curve.

slides.title: Example: trim to the RSL span
slides.head: SKI_PROFILE (grey) trimmed to the span of RSL_Wire (orange), zero at the FCP vertex -- result in blue
slides.body: Trim mode copies the to-edges and cuts them exactly at the two arc lengths; nothing is refitted, so the profile's arcs stay arcs.

keys: The ends of the result (start = the tail end: arc length grows with world X).

items.head: Use Trim for exact results
items.body: It cuts the original edges; lines and arcs keep their type.

items.head: Deform modes are phase 1
items.body: They give the to-chain over the from span, resampled and refitted; carrying geometry that lies off the from-chain is not built yet.

items.head: Arcs only on arc hosts
items.body: Since 2026-09-25 a mapped piece is an arc only where the host is a true arc (M2: R500); on a near-circle spline it stays a spline (M1). Use Recognize arcs to convert splines.
